column1: # lisa curated MITRE ATT&CK mapping subset
# What this is
#   A small, hand-reviewed mapping from lisa correlation rule identifiers
#   to MITRE ATT&CK techniques. It lets a report say which documented technique
#   a configuration weakness is relevant to, using the technique names and
#   tactics published by MITRE.
# What this is not
#   Evidence of adversary activity. A technique listed here describes a
#   documented behaviour an adversary might attempt. A mapping is not evidence
#   that the technique was attempted, that an adversary exists on the host, or
#   that anything was exploited. Only lisa's own observations justify a
#   mapping; the technique names and tactics are the part taken from the ATT&CK
#   catalogue.
# Versioning
#   The dataset_version below is the revision of *this curated subset*, not of
#   MITRE ATT&CK. lisa has no network access and cannot verify the current
#   ATT&CK release, so it deliberately does not assert one. Records should be
#   re-checked against the referenced documentation pages when the subset is next
#   updated, and the technique name or tactic updated if it has changed upstream.
# Attribution
#   Technique names and tactics are (c) The MITRE Corporation. MITRE ATT&CK is
#   published under the Apache License 2.0; terms are at
#   https://attack.mitre.org/resources/terms-of-use/. The mapping choices and the
#   relevance notes are original work by this project.
# Format
#   correlation_rule <TAB> technique_id <TAB> technique_name <TAB> tactic <TAB> reference <TAB> relevance
#   correlation_rule  an LS-COR-* identifier defined in internal/correlation
#   technique_id      ATT&CK technique identifier, validated as T#### or T####.###
#   technique_name    the technique name as published by MITRE
#   tactic            the tactic the technique belongs to, as published
#   reference         documentation location for the technique
#   relevance         why this technique is relevant to the rule's observation,
#                     phrased as a documented possibility and never as a claim
# A rule with no defensible technique is intentionally absent. An unmapped
# correlation is reported without ATT&CK context rather than being given a
# technique chosen to make a report look comprehensive.
# dataset_version: lisa-attack-curated v1
# reviewed_against: MITRE ATT&CK, Enterprise matrix, technique names and tactics as published on the referenced documentation pages
LS-COR-001
column6: A unit or scheduled job that another user can rewrite is a documented way to gain persistence, because the host starts it without operator involvement. The tool observed the writable file and the automatic execution, not an attempt to change either.

column1: LS-COR-002
column6: A setuid or setgid binary whose owner is an unprivileged account combines a documented privilege transition with untrusted control of the file that provides it. The tool observed both properties on one path, not any use of the escalation path.

column1: LS-COR-003
column3: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location
column6: Executables placed in world-writable staging directories are a documented way to have a file appear where an operator expects only data. The tool observed an executable and a payload-shaped artifact in one staging location, and identified neither as malicious.

column1: LS-COR-004
column6: Readable key material combined with a weakened remote access policy is a documented route to credential access. The tool observed both weaknesses; it cannot show that the credentials relate to the access policy, and makes no claim that they were read.
